verifier_note: Checked against ~30 pages of doc.rust-lang.org (Book ch20-01, Reference unsafety/behavior-considered-undefined/operator-expr/tokens/functions, Edition Guide x5, rustc lint listings, std::ptr/hint/mem/ffi docs, Cargo book x2, Nomicon FFI, unstable-book, check-cfg), 6 official Rust release posts (1.77/1.78/1.81/1.82/1.84/1.85), the Miri README (rendered + raw), 3 clippy lint source files plus the clippy README, bindgen/cbindgen plus cbindgen's raw CHANGES, docs.rs for rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 at the pinned version, the Tree Borrows PLDI-2025 abstract page, and the live si-rpg-engine main branch via read-only gh api (solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs, Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, docs/rust-kb-requests.md). I also compiled 71 of the lane's 72 checks myself against the pinned rustc 1.98.1 (plus rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 for the two dependent checks, and wasm32-unknown-unknown+node for the wasm ones) in my own scratch harness, then re-ran all 27 checks a mid-task file regeneration added no_warnings/wasm_no_imports gates to (verified the regeneration was real and narrowly-scoped via hash/line-count/structural diff before trusting it) -- every one passed exactly as the recipe claims. Nothing failed: every API, lint name, error code, attribute, target name and stabilization-version claim matched current docs; every engine_note matched the live repo down to exact function names, constant values (BODY_STRIDE 17, COLLIDER_STRIDE 10, panic=abort in Cargo.toml, edition 2021) and even an approximate line count (the 'step' unsafe block is ~124 lines against a claimed '~120'); and recipe 10's central claim -- that invalid_reference_casting catches a single-expression &T-to-&mut T cast but not the same UB split across a field-write or a Vec-of-pointers hop -- reproduced exactly and matches solver_clear_warmstart's real code byte-for-byte, including the docs.rs proof that rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 has no contact_pairs_mut (E0599) and a private contact_graph (E0616). Systemic weakness: the lane's two formal-aliasing-model PDF sources (Tree Borrows full text, Stacked Borrows POPL'20) could not be text-extracted by any tool available to me here (no local PDF renderer for the Read tool, and WebFetch cannot decode either paper's compressed PDF streams), so recipe 10's deepest theoretical grounding rests on secondary corroboration (the PLDI conference abstract page and a co-author's own blog post) rather than a directly-quoted primary sentence -- everything else in the lane, including that recipe's own practical/code claims, cleared full direct retrieval or direct compilation.
